extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, marketers, communications teams, startup founders, and anyone writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing, formatting, and distributing newsworthy press releases (news releases) intended for journalists and public audiences, with templates for multiple announcement types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness / Show the "So, what?"
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists always need to answer the “So, what?” about a story — in other words, why should their readers care?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out why readers should care, localize national stories for regional outlets, provide local data/angles, and use newsjacking to connect your announcement to current events so it answers both “So, what?” and “Why now?”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Most press releases are succinct, just one to two pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases short and scannable; use bullets for facts/figures and avoid long intros or fluffy background information that reporters don't have time to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia (images, video, infographics) with your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather several high-quality images and, when possible, a video. TV stations need strong visuals; infographics/data visualizations increase pickup. Statistics cited: providing multimedia assets makes journalists more likely to pick up a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline and lede must summarize and use action verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: The heading should contain action verbs, and the first paragraph should answer the who, what, why, and where of your news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a compelling headline that grabs attention and summarizes the key news; lead with most critical information (who, what, when, where, why) using the reverse pyramid so reporters can quickly use your facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release structural format
rubrics_metrics.description: Common format: Contact information and ‘For Immediate Release’ at the top; Title and italicized subheading; A dateline; Opening line sharing the key details; Two to three paragraphs of context; Bulleted facts/figures; Company boilerplate at the bottom; Three pound symbols (###) at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format the release in a newsy, straightforward way so a journalist can imagine it as an article. Use the structural elements to make information easy to find and to signal the end of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential elements to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should include: contact information, the phrase “For immediate release”, a dateline (city and state in all caps followed by release date), a concise headline, business location in the first sentence, a boilerplate, and a signifier like “###”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place contact info at the top or bottom (below boilerplate). Ensure dateline and business location conventions are followed so journalists can quickly contextualize the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing in AP Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Format writing in AP (Associated Press) Style to make it easy for news outlets to pick up your piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP grammar rules, city and state abbreviations, address formatting, title formatting, and rules for spelling out or using figures for numbers. Use online cheat sheets or a searchable AP Style guide as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal vs. informal voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional press releases are third-person; however, active voice and first person (I/We) can personalize your brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose voice based on occasion, industry, and brand — formal (third-person) suits investor disclosures and finance; informal/active can be more trustworthy and fit some brands. Find the right balance for your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse pyramid / strong lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the reverse pyramid formula: most important information first, then less important details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First paragraph: who/what/where; second paragraph: why. Reporters want crisp facts they can use immediately rather than long background. If a colleague can’t explain the news after one read, rewrite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A headline should grab attention and summarize the key news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use action verbs, avoid vague words like “exciting”, be specific, keep it short, and make it interesting. Use data or connections to current events; be playful if it fits the brand and topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The subheadline adds context to the headline and gives readers a better idea of the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand slightly but keep it tight; it can be a short paragraph or bullet points and should support the headline. If stuck, use a placeholder and return later or use the “So, what?” exercise to clarify the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include at least one usable quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes that reporters can use for context and to paint a picture of how the news affects stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose who to quote intentionally (CEO, founder, project lead) and prefer action words while avoiding jargon and hyperbole. A customer quote can be more powerful than a bland executive quote. Provide quotes that add personality and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the “who” and the “what” of your company in a short boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate under 100 words, use clear plain language, and include a link to your website. Place it at the end of the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for reporters to reach you by including full contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a name, title, phone number, and email below the boilerplate so reporters can request additional details, interviews, or visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread and test clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your press release before distribution to avoid typos and formatting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a colleague read it cold; if they can’t explain the news after one read, rewrite. Use tools (including AI) to ideate, write, and edit, but ensure human review for clarity and professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Launch press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Product launches should emphasize the product's specs, pricing, availability, and other details valuable to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convince a journalist why they and their readers should care: share what the product does, its features, pricing, availability date, where it can be purchased, and how it solves a problem. Use credible research to position the problem then show the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mergers & Acquisitions press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational change announcements should inform stakeholders about the growth and trajectory of a company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details about all organizations involved, information about the merger/acquisition, and quotes from leadership teams so stakeholders understand the rationale and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Update press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Product updates and expansions should explain what the change is, why it was made, and how it benefits the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat updates like mini launches: explain the change clearly, emphasize benefits, and include customer or executive quotes that demonstrate real-world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotions press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional press releases can be useful but should be selective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a few big promotions each quarter; don’t send a release for every small discount. Journalists will stop opening your emails if you over-send promotional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Event press releases should give details to attract promotion from news outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include what the event is about, who should consider attending, when and where it will be held, and pricing/ticketing information. State clearly why the event matters to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand Opening press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grand opening releases publicize new locations, relocations, or first-time openings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce date and location, who is involved, any freebies or activities, and the reason for the move if applicable. Make specifics about activities and incentives clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnership announcements should explain the collaboration and benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a summary about each company/person, why the partnership was created, who benefits, and key details; coordinate with the partner on content, approvals, and include quotes/boilerplates from both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebranding press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebranding announcements should explain what changed and why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the change, the reasoning behind it, and why it matters to stakeholders. Tie in executive quotes and use the opportunity to reintroduce your values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership change press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive/team changes should be handled concisely and neutrally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, give a high-level reason for the change, keep the tone neutral, share interim leadership details, provide biographical information to establish credibility, and include a photo and other pertinent details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards press release guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Award announcements should explain the recognition and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information about the company and why they received the award, details about the award itself, and ceremony information if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics (wire, email, owned media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose distribution channels: wire services, targeted email, or owned media posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services offer broad distribution and geographic/industry targeting; email allows customized pitches to specific journalists; owned media (website/social) boosts SEO and reaches existing audiences. Use a mix suited to your goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted journalist outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on specific journalists who are a good fit rather than blasting every contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize pitches, connect the dots for the reporter (explain why the story fits their audience), and demonstrate you understand their beat to increase pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes and exclusives
rubrics_metrics.description: You can send embargoed releases or offer exclusives to give journalists time to craft stories or offer first access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes to allow journalists time to prepare a story; offer exclusives selectively to give outlets first access or special interviews. Clearly state embargo terms and timing in the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and staggered release times
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid publishing on the hour when many releases go out; choose a distinct time and consider time zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select non-standard times (e.g., 1:12 p.m.) to avoid getting lost in the shuffle. Earlier is usually better than later, especially when targeting East Coast/European markets from the West Coast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplify by sharing media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: After pickup, amplify and share media coverage to create a second wave of distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post coverage on social and email to increase reach and help the journalist's metrics; sharing coverage helps both your brand and the journalist and may improve future relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates but customize (avoid cookie-cutter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates provide structure but should be personalized so you don’t sound like everyone else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates to ensure inclusion of essential elements, but make releases unique with new data, remarkable graphics, shareable content, creative angles, and brand personality to increase newsworthiness and pickup.
